paras: The Vineland street fight of 1903 was a clash on the night of July 26, 1903, in Vineland, New Jersey, in which a crowd knocked down a Black police officer, John Shockley, and struck and chased a Black man named Thomas. No one was killed, and the officer, Thomas and a man named Tony Robinson were all arrested. The Bridgeton Pioneer reported it as a "race clash" that "nearly resulted in a riot."

According to a Vineland dispatch dated July 27, Shockley, "a colored officer," and Thomas tried to separate Albey Welser and Harry Loper, who were wrestling on a street corner. Shockley was told to leave them alone but persisted, saying he was stopping a disturbance of the peace, and a bystander struck him and knocked him down. When he got up, Shockley fired his revolver at Tony Robinson and missed, and Robinson knocked him down.

Thomas then pushed through a crowd of about 500, and Loper broke a chair over his head as he passed. Amid what the paper called "the cries of the mob for his life," Thomas ran up the street and escaped through the yard of the Unitarian Church two blocks away.

Robinson was arrested for assaulting the officer and pleaded not guilty the next morning, while Shockley was arrested for shooting at Robinson and Thomas was locked up when he appeared in the city. At the hearing several witnesses testified that Shockley had been drinking, and the paper added that he was already under bonds to keep the peace in two other cases. No report of the outcome of any of the charges was found.

The only known account ran on the front page of the Bridgeton Pioneer on July 30 under the headline "Vineland Has Race Clash." The paper described a "general fight between whites and blacks" but laid its cause to the officer's "interference," gave Welser and Loper's statement that they were "simply having a little fun," and said hundreds who saw the affair sympathized with "the boys."
Shockley said the two youths were fighting, while Welser and Loper said they were only having fun, and both versions come from the same report.

accounts.label: Bridgeton Pioneer's Vineland dispatch
accounts.gist: Shockley's interference with two wrestling youths set off a fight between whites and Blacks; a bystander knocked him down, he fired at Robinson, and Thomas was hit with a chair and chased by the mob.

accounts.label: Officer Shockley
accounts.gist: As reported, he said he was doing his duty in stopping Welser and Loper from disturbing the peace by fighting.

accounts.label: Welser and Loper
accounts.gist: They said they were only having fun, not fighting.

accounts.label: Witnesses at the hearing
accounts.gist: Several testified that Shockley was under the influence of liquor when he came into the city that night.

framing.detail: Called it a 'race clash' and said Thomas 'barely escap[ed] with his life', but traced the trouble to the Black officer's 'interference', reported his drinking and peace bonds, and said hundreds sympathized with the white youths.

versions.value: Welser and Loper were fighting and disturbing the peace (Shockley's account)
Welser and Loper were only having fun, not fighting (their account)

conflicts.note: Both versions appear in the same single report; neither is independently confirmed.

record_check.dossier: John Shockley and Thomas, the two Black men attacked; Robinson was the man Shockley fired at, who then knocked Shockley down, and was charged with assaulting the officer. His race is not stated.
Black: Shockley is 'a colored officer' and Thomas 'a colored man'
Beating and pursuit of Black men; the only shooting was by the Black officer Shockley at Robinson, a miss
Thomas hit over the head with a chair and Shockley knocked down; no injuries are described or counted

info: Night of July 26, 1903 ('last night' in a dispatch dated July 27)
A street corner in Vineland; Thomas fled up the street through the yard of the Unitarian Church two blocks away
John Shockley, a 'colored officer', knocked down by a bystander and then by Tony Robinson; Thomas, 'a colored man', hit over the head with a chair and chased by the crowd
None against the Black men before the fight; Shockley had tried to stop Albey Welser and Harry Loper wrestling on the corner as a disturbance of the peace

An unnamed bystander who knocked Shockley down; Tony Robinson, who knocked Shockley down after Shockley fired at him; Harry Loper, who broke a chair over Thomas's head; and a 'mob' that cried for Thomas's life
No report of the outcome of the charges against Robinson, Shockley or Thomas was found

sources.note: 'Vineland Has Race Clash', dated Vineland July 27: Black officer Shockley shot at Tony Robinson, was knocked down; crowd of about 500; Thomas hit with a chair and chased; arrests and hearing. Only report found.
quotes: A general fight between whites and blacks which nearly resulted in a riot, was occasioned here last night by the interference of John Shockley, a colored officer
Thomas, amid the cries of the mob for his life, rushed up the street and disappeared through the yard of the Unitarian Church, two blocks away, barely escaping with his life.
Hundreds who saw the affair are in sympathy with the boys.
